take: Strait of Hormuz disruption remains the dominant crude driver, with China's 2Q26 import drop confirming demand destruction from higher prices even as US supply cushions the shock. The Jones Act waiver talk is politically motivated but unlikely to move gasoline prices materially above $4, keeping product cracks supported. Product tanker equities are in focus after Brookfield took indirect control of a 19.86% Torm stake, whilst capesize rates show strength with Diana Shipping locking in a $30,500/day fixture, up 18%. Bunker quality is a sleeper risk: high phenolic compound levels up to 15,750 ppm in Chinese ports point to off-spec blends that could destabilise storage and hit engine performance. Watch for any Iran/Oman traffic management deal progress and its impact on Hormuz risk premium, plus US jobs data for macro direction into the week.
